rows.q: How much notice do I need to give before moving out?
rows.answer: You need to give the Landlord at least thirty (30) days' written notice before vacating at the end of the term [§14]. However, for renewal, you must give written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the current term [§13].

rows.q: Can my landlord come in whenever they want?
rows.answer: The lease says the management will provide at least twenty-four (24) hours' notice before entering, except in an emergency [§A2]. However, the landlord may enter the unit at any time upon reasonable notice for specific reasons [§9].

rows.q: Will I get my whole deposit back?
rows.answer: You will have a cleaning fee of $300 deducted from your security deposit at move-out [§5]. This cleaning fee is non-refundable no matter the condition of the unit [§5].

rows.q: What happens if I pay rent a few days late?
rows.answer: If rent is not received by the 5th day of the month, you will pay a late fee of $150, plus $15 per day until it is paid in full [§4]. However, rent received after the 3rd day of the month is considered late and subject to late charges [§A3].

No pets are allowed without the Landlord's prior written consent [§10]. If a pet is approved, there is a pet rent of $50 per month and a non-refundable pet fee of $400 [§10]. You will need to get written consent from the Landlord to have a cat [§10].

rows.q: What if I need to break the lease?
rows.answer: You can end the lease early by giving sixty (60) days' written notice [§12]. You will also have to pay an early termination fee equal to two (2) months' rent [§12].

rows.q: Is there a parking spot included?
rows.answer: (no matching clause; the app answers "The lease doesn't mention that" without calling Gemma)
This Lease will automatically renew for twelve (12) month terms. Either you or the landlord must give written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the current term ends.
You have to pay a security deposit of $2,150. There is a non-refundable cleaning fee of $300 that will be taken out of your deposit when you move out.
The landlord can enter your unit anytime if they give you reasonable notice. They can do this to inspect, make repairs, or show the unit to new tenants.
